summary: Reviewed the D.110c-0b0b section (plan lines 93065-93222, with 0b umbrella context at 91736-91888) against the local sources it cites. Note on authentication: no shell/git tool was available and the worktree gitdir is outside my permitted read scope, so I authenticated the checkpoint from the supplied clean detached checkout (HEAD 22917252, parent 2b3080d6, clean status) and reviewed its content; the tree SHA was not independently recomputable. Claim 1 is verified real: openCurrentAnchorTrust rejects any record with currentEpoch !== 0 or currentAnchorDigest !== genesisAnchorDigest (packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:1437-1438,1404-1405); successor minting is symbol-keyed private custody requiring an already-held predecessor capability (index.ts:1668-1717, internal/seal-authority-custody.ts, not in package.json exports), so Node cannot mint epoch-N trust privately; and inspectCreatorTrustAdvance's exactCombinedClosure removes only the old trust ref and appends the new trust plus two proof refs, retaining every earlier CutValue/QC pair (packages/control-plane/src/creator-trust-advance.ts:88-99,161-167) — the O(N) owner. The selected boundaries are non-root additions consistent with existing subpath precedent (protocol-v3 ./creator-close, control-plane ./creator-trust-advance) and add no wire field, record version, dependency, threshold, authority, or migration; root rosters (protocol-v3 package.json smoke:public-package) are untouched. The opener's authentication statement is non-circular: the predecessor is pinned by the authenticated current anchor's previousAnchor, and the QC is intrinsically bound to the predecessor's (objectId, epoch) via openSealAuthority/verifySealQC (seal.ts:303-321,450-460) with the cut fixed by successorAnchor byte equality (creator-close.ts:203-225,632-637); requiring the predecessor is conservative rather than unsafe, so criterion 3 yields no P1. Freshness honesty, archive separation, TDD ordering (0b0b design acceptance before a/b product RED, 0b1 RED/GREEN on the genuine 0->1->2 path), and the limited Hiero/WRAPS conclusion are internally consistent; upstream clones were not re-readable under this permission scope and the mechanical refresh was not required. One blocking gap remains: the frozen opener's first input (a pin-authenticated epoch-0 genesisTrust) has no named source that survives the design's own retention law at epoch N>=2.

findings.title: Frozen epoch-N opener requires an epoch-0 genesisTrust with no named source beyond epoch 1
findings.evidence: Plan 93096-93100 makes 'one already pin-authenticated epoch-0 genesisTrust' the first closed input, and 93140-93145 states active epoch N retains only the current trust record plus the N-1->N Cut/QC and two Superseded rollback generations. Minting that capability requires the full epoch-0 trust-state record bytes (packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:1375-1405). The only production owner of those bytes is the epoch-0 generation closure (packages/control-plane/src/anchor-trust.ts:535-612 install/openAtHead), and control-plane forbids a second trust record per closure (anchor-trust.ts:404-406 'trust-state-ambiguous'), so genesis cannot ride along in the active closure. Per the real lineage used by cold reopen (packages/node/src/creator-adoption.ts:914-962), each transition advances two generations (adoption, then successor-live), so at epoch 2 the retained window is live(2)/adoption(2)/live(1) and the genesis generation and its blob are outside the active+two-Superseded window and eligible for deletion (packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:270-341; packages/storage/src/maintenance.ts:404-433 with deleteBlobDigests). Existing production caller input carries only the genesis anchor preimage and its signature (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:134-143,2156-2178), not the assembled record. Plan 91760-91761 (0b) conversely asserts the active generation retains both a genesis and a current trust record, which the unchanged inspectTrustClosure rejects; 0b0b keeps that function unchanged (91801-91804).
findings.required_action: Documentation-only correction to the frozen 0b0b contract (no API/wire/authority widening): name the O(1) owner and retention/delivery path of the pinned genesis carrier at epoch N>=2 — either (a) an explicitly retained durable epoch-0 trust-state blob added to the retention law and the D.110c-c/d durable census, or (b) reduce the frozen input to the already caller-held pinned genesis anchor preimage plus the profile/signer-set carriers taken from the authenticated records, stating explicitly why carrier substitution is safe (genesis anchor commits profileDigest/signerSetDigest and its digest equals the pin) — and reconcile the 91760-91761 wording with the enforced one-trust-record closure law.

findings.title: Predecessor-location sentence is off-by-one and the window margin is unstated
findings.evidence: Plan 93143-93145 says the immediate predecessor trust record 'resides in the newest of exactly two complete Superseded rollback generations'. Per packages/node/src/creator-adoption.ts:919-946 the predecessor trust record is read from currentGeneration, the older of the two retained Superseded closures (the newest Superseded holds the current trust plus the transition pair), and packages/node/src/internal/closed-epoch-cleanup.ts:279-297 retains exactly active plus two Superseded, leaving zero margin against any additional head-advancing generation.
findings.required_action: Restate the law with the exact generation-to-epoch mapping and the load-bearing invariant it depends on (bounded head-advancing generations per epoch; reclamation may never evict the closure carrying the immediate predecessor trust record). Disposition owner: D.110c-0b1 GREEN retention law, with the census carried into D.110c-c/d.

findings.title: Opener statement omits explicit objectId and genesisAnchorDigest equality across the three records
findings.evidence: Plan 93101-93108 requires byte-identical profile/signer-set carriers, both creator signatures, adjacent epochs, previous-anchor linkage, cut/QC, successor derivation, and the copied expected tuple, but never states objectId or genesisAnchorDigest equality between genesisTrust, the predecessor record, and the current record. Both existing precedents check them (packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:1403-1405; packages/protocol-v3/src/creator-close.ts:596-597), and the adversarial gate list at 93170-93171 assumes cross-room/cross-genesis rejection.
findings.required_action: Add the two explicit equalities (objectId and genesisAnchorDigest of both records equal to the genesis trust material) to the frozen authentication statement and to the 0b1 RED vectors. Disposition owner: D.110c-0b0b design text, enforced by D.110c-0b1 RED.

findings.title: Bounded advance accepts caller-declared retiring refs without a stated derivation binding
findings.evidence: Plan 93113-93122 defines inspectBoundedCreatorTrustAdvance as a structural delta over {current,proofRefs,proposed,retiringProofRefs} after the Node/protocol owner 'has identified the current transition pair'; 'non-current' rejection is not defined, and refs alone cannot distinguish a transition pair from any other preserved ref. Closure candidates already carry scannable bytes for every ref (packages/control-plane/src/anchor-trust.ts:390-406), so kind/epoch confirmation is available.
findings.required_action: State that retiringProofRefs must be derived from the digests of the authenticated prior-transition CutValue/commit-QC bytes, and/or that the predicate confirms via candidates that they decode to exactly one drp-hard-epoch-cut and one drp-seal-qc bound to the retiring epoch. Disposition owner: D.110c-0b1 GREEN (control-plane boundary plus Node composition).
